intro.note: Answer each question in your workbook. Show your working.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to halve the second difference.
Not finding the linear part correctly.
Sign errors with a negative linear part.
intro.visualAid: A quadratic sequence has a constant SECOND difference. Halving it gives the coefficient of n²; subtracting the an² values leaves a simpler linear sequence to finish the rule.

questions.content: Find first and second differences: a) 2, 5, 10, 17, 26  b) 4, 7, 12, 19, 28
Quadratic? Show second differences: a) 1, 4, 9, 16  b) 2, 4, 6, 8
nth term = n² + n. a) 1st term  b) 5th term  c) 10th term
Tile pattern: 2, 6, 12, 20, … a) Tiles in pattern 5. b) nth term.
Sequence 1, 6, 15, 28, 45. a) Show second difference constant. b) nth term. c) 10th term.
nth term = n² − 3n + 2. a) First four terms. b) Show 2nd difference is 2. c) Which term = 30?
